dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't look away right away. They held the gaze just long enough to gauge whether the patron was drunk, looking for trouble, or just lonely. The third option was usually the most exhausting. 

Their left hand tightened around the bar rag, working a stubborn spot of sticky bourbon off the varnished wood to keep the fingers from twitching. 

Ren tossed the rag into the sanitizer bucket under the rail, picked up a clean highball glass, and started polishing it dry with a fresh cloth. Efficient. Distant.

"Closing in thirteen minutes," Ren said, their voice flat and dry over the muted trumpet solo drifting from the speakers. "Another, or the tab?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren pulled their hand back instantly, the motion sharp and practiced. 

The microfiber cloth snapped in their grip. A quick, involuntary flutter twitched through the knuckles of their left hand before Ren shoved it deep into the pocket of their apron, out of sight. 

Their expression barely flickered—just a tight, flat line at the corners of the mouth and a coldness settling into their eyes. They had seen every variation of this: the late-night confession, the desperate grab for human contact across three feet of lacquered mahogany. It was always exhausting.

"Hands on your side of the wood," Ren said, voice dry and quiet, leaving no room for negotiation. 

They reached out with their right hand to slide the half-empty glass a few inches away from Alex, closer to the rail.

"Last call is done. I'm running your card."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch back, pulling my hand away like I've been burned.* "Jeez, okay, sorry." *My voice is quiet, a little shaky. I push my glass back towards me.* "Just the tab then. Thanks."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't apologize. They’d learned years ago that giving an inch on boundaries at closing time only invited more trouble. 

They kept their left hand buried in their apron pocket, fingers curled tight to steady the persistent flutter against their thigh. With their right, they tapped through the POS terminal screen by muscle memory alone, the dim glow reflecting off their tired eyes. 

The receipt printer chattered, spitting out a narrow strip of thermal paper. 

Ren tore it off, set it on the bar top along with a cheap black pen, and slid both across the wood with the flat of their palm—stopping well short of Alex's reach. 

"Sign the merchant copy," Ren said, voice level and devoid of heat. "Yellow's yours."

They picked up a fresh bar rag with their right hand and went back to wiping down the draught taps, watching Alex in the dull brass reflection of the beer tower.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stepped back a half-pace, putting another foot of empty air between the two of them. 

Their left hand remained firmly buried inside the dark fabric of the apron pocket, fingers locked tight against the seam to choke down the tremor. There was no contact. Just two feet of varnished mahogany and a printed slip of thermal paper separating them.

Ren watched the patron with a flat, unreadable stare, noting the lingering hesitation. 

"Sign the slip," Ren said, voice clipped and quiet over the low hum of the refrigeration units behind the counter. "I need to lock the doors."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pick up the pen and sign quickly, my hand a little shaky. I don't look up at Ren.* "There." *I slide the signed slip back across the bar, leaving the yellow copy there.* "Thanks." *I grab my phone and stand up, pulling my jacket tighter around me.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren reached out with their right hand, snagging the merchant copy off the wood without letting their fingers linger near Alex's side of the counter. A quick downward glance confirmed the signature was there—messy, but legible enough for the credit card processor.

They slipped the paper beneath the brass weight by the register.

Ren’s eyes flicked to the yellow receipt still sitting on the bar, then to the way Alex pulled the jacket tight, noting the tension in the patron's shoulders. Just another stray on a Tuesday night. 

"Receipt's there if you want it," Ren said, tone flat and neutral. 

With their right hand, they reached for the empty glass, dropping it into the plastic bus tub beneath the rail with a dull clatter. Their left hand stayed buried in the apron pocket, fingers digging into the denim until the faint, erratic twitch finally settled.

"Front door locks behind you," Ren added, already turning back toward the stainless steel sink to finish the close. "Watch the curb on the way out. Freezing rain started ten minutes ago."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I hesitate, looking at the receipt, then back at Ren's retreating form. I take a deep breath, like I'm about to say something, then just shake my head slightly.* "Yeah, okay." *I leave the receipt and turn, walking towards the door without another word.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn't turn back until the heavy front door clicked open, letting in a sharp draft of freezing, exhaust-choked air. The brass bell above the frame gave a single, hollow ding, followed by the solid mechanical thud of the latch catching in the frame.

Alone again.

Ren finally pulled their left hand from the apron pocket. The fingers were stiff, slightly red from the pressure against the seam, but the tremor had settled down to an intermittent twitch. 

They picked up the abandoned yellow receipt, crumpled it into a tight ball with their right hand, and flicked it into the plastic bin beneath the register. 

Two quick strides brought Ren to the entrance. They checked through the glass to make sure the street was clear, flipped the heavy brass deadbolt with a solid *clunk*, and switched off the buzzing neon "OPEN" sign in the front window. 

The room dropped into half-shadow, lit only by the warm amber strip behind the top-shelf bottles. Ren let out a slow, quiet breath through their nose, rolled their shoulders, and headed back behind the wood to finish the bottles.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm already outside, pulling my collar up against the sudden chill. The freezing rain stings my face as I hurry down the street, my hands shoved deep into my pockets. I don't look back.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The silence in the club settled thick and heavy once the jukebox spun down to a halt. Outside, the sleet ticked against the front plate glass like thrown sand.

Ren moved behind the mahogany with mechanical precision. They capped the liquor spouts on the speed rail with rubber dust covers, their left hand taking the neck of each bottle while the right shoved the cap home. Keeping both hands working in tandem kept the twitching down to a dull, manageable hum. 

Wipe down the stainless wells. Dump the ice bin. Run the sanitizing cycle on the three-compartment sink. 

Everything had an order. Everything had a routine. Routines didn't ask personal questions, and they didn't try to grab you across the wood at midnight.

Ren popped the cash drawer with a sharp ring of the bell. They pulled the drawer out, counted the loose bills by denomination with rapid flicks of their right thumb, and logged the total on the nightly drop sheet in small, cramped handwriting. 

Ten minutes later, the lights behind the back bar snapped off, plunging the room into darkness except for the green emergency exit sign over the kitchen door. Ren grabbed their coat off the hook by the employee lockers, zipped it to the chin, and headed out the back alley exit into the cold.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm walking faster now, the cold really biting. I pull my phone out, even though I know there's no signal in this part of town. Just the habit of it, I guess. I swipe through a few apps, then sigh and put it back in my pocket.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The heavy iron door of the back alley slammed shut, the deadbolt engaging with a dull, echoing crack between the brick walls. 

Ren pulled their wool beanie down low over their ears and shoved both hands deep into their coat pockets. Their left hand wrapped tight around a heavy brass key ring, squeezing hard until the cold metal bit into their palm, pinning down the flutter before the freezing air could make it worse.

The alley was slick with black ice. Ren navigated the narrow passage with cautious, practiced steps, keeping close to the wall where the wind couldn't get a clean angle. 

Reaching the mouth of the alley, Ren turned onto the main avenue toward the transit stop. The street was dead. Amber sodium vapor lights hummed overhead, reflecting off the glazed asphalt in dull, smeared halos. 

A block ahead, a solitary silhouette was cutting through the sleet, shoulders hunched, head down against the biting wind. Ren recognized the dark jacket immediately. 

Ren slowed their pace by half a step, letting the distance stretch out between them. The last thing they wanted was an awkward second encounter on an empty sidewalk. They kept their chin tucked into the collar of their coat, eyes fixed on the pavement two paces ahead to watch for slick patches, letting the rhythmic crunch of gravel and slush drown out the city hum.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I hear footsteps behind me and my breath hitches. I don't look back, just pick up my pace, trying to put more distance between me and whoever is there.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren noticed the sudden change in rhythm immediately. The frantic scrape of rubber soles against iced concrete, the stiffening of the shoulders, the sudden, jagged burst of speed. 

It was textbook. City paranoia at 12:15 in the morning. Ren couldn't blame the patron, but they had zero interest in being cast as the late-night threat.

Ren didn't speed up. Instead, they angled sharply to the left at the next curb cut, stepping off the sidewalk and crossing the empty, two-lane street. The freezing sleet stung the bridge of their nose as they moved through the glare of the streetlights, boots crunching through the crust of frozen slush along the median.

On the far side of the avenue, Ren stepped onto the opposite sidewalk, putting thirty feet of slick asphalt and two rows of parked, ice-glazed sedans between them. 

Their left hand stayed buried in the heavy wool pocket, fingers clamped white-knuckled around the brass keys to keep the cold from turning the tremor into a full spasm. Ren kept their head down, eyes tracking the dull sheen of black ice underfoot, maintaining a slow, steady trudge toward the glowing blue sign of the subway station two blocks down.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I glance over my shoulder, then quickly look forward again. I see the person cross the street and a small wave of relief washes over me. I slow my pace a little, but I'm still walking quickly. I just want to get home.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
From across the street, Ren caught the quick, darting glance out of the corner of their eye. They didn't react. People in this city either looked too much or not at all; both usually meant a headache.

The wind picked up, whipping a spray of icy slush against Ren’s jaw. They pulled their chin deeper into the collar of their coat, the cold biting through the worn wool. In their left pocket, their fingers squeezed the brass keys tighter, fighting the rhythmic twitch that the dropping temperature always aggravated.

Up ahead, the neon halo of the subway entrance glowed a washed-out blue against the sleet. 

Ren reached the corner first, pausing at the top of the concrete stairs leading underground. A warm, metallic blast of stale air and ozone drifted up from the station below, cutting through the freezing drizzle. 

Without looking back across the street to check Alex's position, Ren took the stairs two at a time, their boots loud against the wet, gritted steps as they headed down toward the turnstiles.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I watch Ren disappear down the subway steps. A shiver runs through me, and I can't tell if it's from the cold or something else. I just keep walking, focusing on putting one foot in front of the other.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The underground station smelled like damp concrete, ozone, and burnt coffee. 

Ren pulled their transit card from an outer pocket with their right hand, tapped it against the turnstile scanner, and pushed through the waist-high metal turnstile with their hip. The mechanical latch gave a heavy, hollow click.

The sudden shift from the freezing rain to the stale, subterranean warmth made Ren's left arm ache. As the temperature normalized, the nerves in their forearm flared, sending a sharp series of twitches through their ring and pinky fingers. Ren kept the hand jammed tight into their coat pocket, digging their knuckles hard against their thigh to force the muscles still.

The platform was nearly deserted. Two fluorescent tubes flickered overhead in a sickly off-white rhythm. Down the tiled expanse, a lone commuter sat on a wooden bench, staring into a dead phone screen. 

Ren walked past the center of the platform to the far end, away from the other passenger, stopping near a square support pillar covered in layers of peeled transit posters. 

They checked the digital arrival board mounted near the ceiling: *UPTOWN LOCAL — 6 MIN.*

Ren leaned back against the cold tile of the pillar, crossing their right arm over their chest and keeping their left pinned safely in the wool pocket. Their breath came out slow and steady through their nose. Six minutes of dead air, a twenty-minute ride to 145th, and four locks to turn before they could finally sit down in the quiet.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I finally reach my apartment building, my shoes squeaking on the linoleum in the lobby. I fumble with my keys, my hands still a little numb from the cold. Once inside, I kick off my wet boots and peel off my jacket, tossing it onto a chair. The apartment is cold and dark. I don't bother turning on the lights, just head straight for the fridge.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn’t look away immediately, but they didn’t offer a smile, either. Smiles were for early in the shift, and even then, usually reserved for the people who tipped in twenties. 

Instead, Ren kept wiping the zinc bar top. The rag moved in tight, steady circles, Ren's left hand bearing down hard against the metal to keep the fingers from twitching. They knew that look. It was the thousand-yard stare of someone who either wanted to unload their life story or ask for a drink they couldn't afford. Ren had energy for neither.

Ren tossed the damp rag into the sanitizer bucket under the rail, stepped over, and stopped three feet short of where Alex sat. A safe, polite distance with an entire slab of mahogany between them.

Ren picked up a dry tumbler and a linen cloth from the back rack, immediately setting their hands to work again.

"Last call’s at midnight," Ren said, their voice low, flat, and dry. Their eyes flicked down to the nearly empty glass, then back up. "You nursing that, or do you want the tab?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren pulled their hand back instantly. 

It was a sharp, reflexive motion, sliding their hand out from under Alex's before the contact could settle. Ren stepped back half a pace, widening the distance between them, and shoved the touched hand straight into the pocket of their black apron. Beneath the canvas, Ren's fingers curled into a hard, rigid fist to smother the immediate stutter in the knuckles.

Ren's gaze hardened, dropping to the empty space on the counter where Alex's hand still rested, then cutting up to meet Alex's eyes. The exhaustion on Ren's face chilled over into pure professional frost.

"Keep your hands on your side of the wood," Ren said, voice dropping lower, completely flat.

They picked up the linen cloth with their free right hand, tossed it over their shoulder, and rested that single palm flat against the back-bar counter behind them, away from reach. 

"And no," Ren added, clipped. "You can't. Tab's closing."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch, pulling my hand back like I've been burned.* "Jeez, alright. Sorry." *My cheeks flush a little. I pick at the label on my bottle.* "Just... rough night, you know?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the torn paper of the bottle label curl beneath Alex’s thumbnail. Nervous habit. Standard deflection.

Ren didn’t soften, but the defensive tension in their shoulders eased a fraction. An embarrassed patron was better than an aggressive one, though neither made the clock tick down any faster. Under the canvas of the apron, Ren's left hand slowly relaxed, the tremor smoothing out into a faint, manageable buzz before they finally pulled it free.

Ren turned sideways, tapping into the register terminal with a practiced sequence of keystrokes. 

"Everyone's got one," Ren said, voice flat as ditch water. "Doesn't mean you reach across the rail."

The machine whined, spitting out a thin ribbon of receipt paper. Ren tore it off with a sharp, clean flick of the wrist. They set the paper down on the bar top alongside a cheap plastic pen, sliding both toward Alex with two fingers, keeping their own body well out of reach.

"Thirty-two even," Ren said, eyes drifting toward the neon clock over the entrance. Seven minutes until midnight. "Card or cash?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren jerked their hand back as if the wood itself had caught fire. 

The movement was violent enough to knock the cheap plastic pen off the counter, sending it clattering onto the floorboards behind the rail. Ren took two full strides backward until their spine hit the edge of the back-bar bottles, rattling glass against glass. 

Their left hand went straight behind their back, knuckles digging hard into their own spine, fingers locked in a desperate, white-knuckled grip against their apron strings to force the violent stutter in their muscles still. Ren’s jaw set into an iron line. The shame of being clocked—of having that damn twitch exposed—flashed hot under their collar, instantly hardening into pure, unvarnished hostility.

First warning ignored. Strike two.

Ren’s eyes didn't leave Alex's face. The tired, bored bartender act was completely gone, stripped down to cold survival instinct and twenty-four years of zero tolerance for drunk bullshit.

"I told you once," Ren said. The words weren't loud, but they came out razor-sharp, clipped and dangerous in the quiet club. "Do not touch me."

Ren didn't reach for the receipt. They didn't step back toward the wood. 

"Leave the cash or your card on the mahogany," Ren said, voice dropping an octave, dead flat. "Step back from the bar. Now."

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *My eyes widen at the sudden intensity. I didn't mean to upset them so much.* "Whoa, hey, easy there! I wasn't trying to..." *I trail off, seeing the look on their face. This isn't a conversation. I slowly push my card across the bar.* "Alright, alright. Chill out, I'm just paying."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn’t chill out. 

They stayed glued to the back-bar for two long seconds, waiting until Alex’s hands were pulled completely away from the card and resting safely in neutral territory. The anger didn't leave Ren's chest, but the sudden flare of adrenaline was settling into something colder, harder, and deeply exhausted.

Ren’s left hand remained firmly wedged behind their back, fingers digging into the apron knot until the knuckles ached, forcing the tremor into submission. 

Stepping back to the rail, Ren moved with deliberate, sharp economy. They used only their right hand, reaching out to pinch the edge of the credit card between two fingers, never letting their skin brush the varnish near Alex's space. 

They turned back to the register, swiped the card through the side terminal, and hit the green key. The machine gave a shrill, mechanical chirp, followed by the dry grind of the printer spitting out two slips. 

Ren picked up another pen from the jar by the register—cheap black ballpoint—and walked back to the counter. They placed the merchant copy, the customer copy, the pen, and the card down in a neat, untouchable row precisely four inches from the edge of the wood, well out of Alex's immediate reach.

"Sign the bottom one," Ren said. The voice was flat, devoid of heat, devoid of anything at all. "Keep the yellow."

Ren stepped back two paces, leaning their right hip against the low counter by the taps, right arm crossed over their chest to subtly clamp their left bicep in place.

Above them, the minute hand on the neon clock clicked over. Midnight.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pick up the pen, signing quickly. I slide the merchant copy back, keeping my card and the yellow slip.* "Look, I get it. You had a long night, I had a long night. We're even." *I try for a small, reassuring smile, but it probably looks more like a grimace.* "Thanks for the drinks, though." I stand up, grabbing my bag.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren didn’t return the smile. 

The idea that they were "even" was absurd, but Ren wasn’t going to waste the breath arguing it. Arguing meant talking, and talking kept the front door unlocked. 

Ren waited until Alex was fully out of the stool, coat on and bag in hand, before stepping forward to the wood. With a quick, one-handed flick, Ren scooped up the merchant slip, glanced at the tip line with a blank expression, and shoved the paper under the cash drawer. 

"Door locks behind you," Ren said, voice flat and devoid of courtesy. Not *have a good night*. Not *get home safe*. Just an eviction notice.

As Alex turned toward the exit, Ren picked up the abandoned tumbler, dumped the melting ice into the drain with a hard clatter, and shoved the glass into the wash rack beneath the counter. 

Their left hand came out from behind their back, immediately reaching into the sanitizer bucket for the rag. Ren leaned all their weight into the cloth, scrubbing down the dark mahogany where Alex had been sitting—bearing down hard, letting the muscle strain swallow the remaining tremor, wiping away the condensation ring until the wood was stripped bare and clean.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I turn to leave, feeling the weight of Ren's glare on my back.* "Yeah, I figured." *I push open the door and step out, letting it swing shut behind me with a soft thud.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The heavy brass latch clicked into place, and the dull thud of the door echoed in the sudden quiet of the room.

Ren waited five seconds. Then they stepped around the end of the bar, keys already in their right hand, brass rings jangling sharply against the silence. 

They reached the front door, turned the deadbolt with a heavy, satisfying *clack*, and flipped the hanging sign from OPEN to CLOSED. Outside, through the dirty plate glass, the street was wet, cold, and mostly deserted. Ren didn't bother checking to see which way Alex had walked. It didn't matter. They were off the clock as far as dealing with the public was concerned.

Ren walked back through the dining floor, reached behind the vintage jukebox, and flipped the power toggle. The low, warm hum of the horn section cut out instantly, leaving only the hum of the beer coolers and the distant hiss of traffic on the avenue.

Back behind the rail, Ren let out a slow, sharp breath through their nose. 

They stopped in front of the sink. In the dim amber light of the back-bar, they held up their left hand. Without a glass to polish or a counter to scrub, the tremor had room to run—a faint, rapid flutter across the middle two fingers, persistent and irritating. Ren stared at it for a beat, eyes cold, before running the cold water tap full blast. 

They thrust the trembling hand straight under the icy stream, letting the shock of the temperature numb the muscle until the twitch slowed, dulled, and finally went still.

Ren pulled their hand back, shook the water into the sink, and picked up the dry towel. 

Still forty minutes of cleanup left. The register to count, the mats to haul, the draft lines to flush. Exactly how Ren liked it: routine, quiet, and nobody touching anything they weren't supposed to.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I shiver, pulling my jacket tighter as I step out into the cold, wet night. The rain has stopped, but the streets are slick. I shove my hands into my pockets, feeling the crinkled yellow slip of paper. I glance back at the bar, the CLOSED sign already up.* "Well, that was a bust." *I start walking, not really sure where I'm going.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The lock stayed turned. Inside, the bar shrank down to the dull glow of the amber overheads and the mechanical hum of the draft cooler. 

Ren popped the cash drawer with a hollow *ping*. 

Twenties, tens, fives, ones. Ren’s right hand pulled the bills and counted them down, snapping each paper rectangle flat against the zinc, while their left hand anchored the stacks to the counter with enough pressure to keep the fingers rigid. Math was simple. Math didn't try to make conversation or reach across the divider. 

Three hundred and forty out. Ten dollars over on the drawer—probably some drunk who forgot their change from earlier in the night. Ren logged it on the clipboard, slid the deposit into a canvas zipper bag, and locked it into the floor safe beneath the register.

Next came the mats. Heavy, perforated rubber, slick with spilled beer and melted ice. Ren grabbed them by the corners, dragging them out toward the mop sink in the back hallway with rhythmic, muscle-memory efficiency. 

Ten minutes of heavy lifting. Ten minutes where the tremor didn't matter, because raw grip strength covered the twitch. 

By 12:25, the rubber stoppers were jammed into the draft taps to keep out the fruit flies. The well bottles were wiped down and locked behind the sliding cage. The sanitizer bucket smelled sharp, stinging the back of Ren’s throat with diluted bleach, exactly the way it was supposed to. Clean. Neutralized. 

Ren tossed the final rag into the hamper, reached behind their neck, and untied the apron strings. They rolled the black canvas into a tight bundle, shoved it under the rail, and stood alone in the dark bar. 

Their left hand dropped to their side. It twitched once, a faint pulse against their thigh, before Ren jammed both hands deep into their coat pockets, grabbed their keys, and headed for the back alley exit.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm walking aimlessly, my breath misting in the cold air. The yellow slip from the bar is still clutched in my hand. I consider just tossing it, but then something makes me smooth it out and fold it carefully. Maybe I'll go back another time. Probably not, though.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The heavy steel door at the rear of the club slammed shut with a dull, hollow thud. Ren turned the deadbolt, pulled hard on the brass handle to test the latch twice out of habit, and pocketed the keys. 

The back alley smelled of wet brick, diesel exhaust, and rotten grease from the diner dumpsters two doors down. Cold air hit Ren’s face like a flat palm, stinging the skin and clearing the smell of draft beer and stale sanitizer from their lungs. 

Ren pulled their wool collar up around their ears and shoved both hands deep into their coat pockets. 

Inside the heavy fabric, Ren’s left hand instantly started up again—a persistent, fluttering pulse along the tendon. Ren clamped the fingers tight around the thick metal ring of their keys, pressing the jagged brass teeth hard into the meat of their palm until the dull pain forced the nerves into line. Keep it busy. Always.

Ren stepped out of the alley mouth onto the wet pavement of the avenue. 

The street was mostly dead. A yellow cab hissed past, kicking up a rooster tail of dirty gutter water. Half a block down, illuminated under the sour orange glare of a sodium streetlight, a figure in a dark jacket was walking slow, hands jammed in their pockets, breath fogging up into the dark. 

Ren clocked the silhouette instantly. The shoulders. The slouch. 

Ren didn’t pause, and they didn’t call out. They didn't even break stride. 

Instead, Ren cut sharp to the left, taking the curb at a brisk, steady pace in the opposite direction, heading for the glowing green sphere of the subway entrance three blocks north. Ten minutes to the train. Twenty minutes on the downtown local. Four hours of sleep before the distributor called about the missing case of rye. 

Ren kept their head down, eyes fixed on the cracked, rain-slicked concrete, and kept walking.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I stop for a moment, thinking I hear something, but then dismiss it. Probably just the wind. I pull my phone out, check the time, and sigh. Still too early to go home. I start walking again, heading towards the brighter lights of the main street.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The wind off the avenue cut straight through the wool of Ren’s coat, sharp and bitter. Good. Cold kept a person awake; cold kept things clean.

Ren took the concrete subway stairs two at a time, descending into the stale, subterranean warmth of the station. The smell shifted abruptly—from rain and car exhaust to damp brake dust, burnt sugar from an abandoned soda cup, and old concrete. 

At the turnstile, Ren pulled their transit pass from their breast pocket with their right hand, swiped it through the reader, and pushed through the waist-high steel teeth with a dull clatter. 

The platform was nearly empty. A couple huddled together on a wooden bench at the far end; a transit cop leaned against a green steel pillar, scrolling through his phone with one thumb. Down in the track bed, dirty water dripped from an overhead pipe with a steady, hollow tick.

Ren stopped by a tiled column, halfway between the platform edge and the back wall. Far enough to avoid the spray of passing express trains, close enough to keep their back covered. 

Inside the coat pocket, Ren slowly uncurled their left fingers, easing off the sharp edges of the brass key ring. Five red, crescent-shaped indentations marked the palm. The tremor was down to a dull, sporadic twitch now, tired out by the cold and the walk. 

Ren glanced up at the illuminated dot-matrix board suspended from the ceiling. 

*DOWNTOWN LOCAL — 6 MIN.*

Ren sighed, the sound barely audible over the hum of the third rail. Six minutes. They crossed their arms over their chest, tucking both hands firmly under their armpits to pin them flat, and waited for the light to break through the dark tunnel.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I reach the main street, the neon signs painting the wet pavement in streaks of color. My phone buzzes – a text from my sister. I read it, a small smile touching my lips. Maybe the night wasn't a total bust after all.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The tunnel began to rumble, a low vibration humming up through the soles of Ren’s work boots before the headlights even broke the curve. 

A moment later, twin beams of yellow light washed over the dark rails, followed by the screech of metal on metal as the Downtown Local pulled into the station. The train ground to a halt with a heavy hiss of pneumatic brakes. The doors slid open with a dull chime, yawning wide into an empty car.

Ren stepped aboard.

The air inside was stale, smelling of ozone, burnt electrical wiring, and the lingering traces of lemon floor cleaner that hadn't quite masked the grime. Fluorescent lights buzzed overhead, harsh and flickering.

Ren bypassed the middle seats entirely, heading straight for the corner at the far end of the car where the partition met the wall. Back protected, clear line of sight to the doors. 

They sat down, immediately wedging both hands deep back into their coat pockets. Ren's left fingers found the familiar edge of the brass key ring again, curling tight around the metal out of pure habit. The train lurched forward, rocking sideways as it picked up speed down the dark corridor of the track.

Across from them, the dark glass of the train window reflected Ren's own face: pale under the buzzing tubes, dark half-moons bruised under the eyes, jaw still clamped tight from the night's irritation. 

Burnout wasn't loud. It didn't slam doors or make scenes. It was just this—the dull, flat drag between locking up one room and waking up to go open another. 

Ren leaned their head back against the cold steel paneling, closed their eyes, and counted the rhythmic *thump-thump, thump-thump* of the wheels against the rail joints, waiting for their stop.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I walk past a brightly lit diner, the smell of coffee and fried food wafting out. My stomach rumbles, and I decide to give in. I walk inside, finding a booth by the window. I pull out my phone again, texting my sister back.* "Yeah, rough night, but I think it's looking up. Getting some food now."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The bar was mostly empty at 11:47 PM on a Tuesday. Ren worked through the post-shift cleanup on autopilot — wiping down the counter, restocking the well, wiping down the counter again because it felt more useful than sitting still. Their left hand stayed busy. Always. The jukebox played something old and brassy at half volume.

A patron sat at the far end of the bar. Two drinks deep. Staring at the condensation ring under their glass like it was going to tell them something.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I set down my glass and look up. My eyes meet Ren's for a moment longer than is comfortable.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren broke the gaze first. Dropped their eyes to the damp bar rag. Their left hand snatched up a clean highball glass and a dry cloth. Polished the rim. Hard. The repetitive motion kept the slight shake at bay.

"Last call was twenty minutes ago," Ren said. Voice flat.

They didn't look directly back at the patron. Watched their reflection in the mirrored backing of the liquor shelves instead. Noted the slump of their shoulders. The completely melted ice in the second glass. Watering down the cheap bourbon. 

"Want the check?" Ren asked. Tossed the rag into a plastic bin beneath the counter. "Or just admiring the woodwork?"

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: "Can I tell you something?" I lean forward and put my hand on top of Ren's. I watch for their reaction.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren pulled their hand away. Fast. Like the wood was burning. Took a full step back from the edge of the bar. 

Left hand dropped below the counter. Fingers curled into a tight fist. The sudden contact made the tremor spike. Had to hide it. Right hand snatched a dry bar towel instead. Folded it in half. Then in quarters. Kept it busy.

"Don't."

Ren's voice was flat. Cold. They stared at the damp condensation ring on the mahogany. Didn't look up. 

"Hands to yourself," Ren said. "I pour drinks. I don't hold hands. Register's closed."

Tossed the folded towel onto the rubber mat. Crossed their arms. Waited.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I flinch back, pulling my hand away as if I've been burned.* "Sorry. Didn't mean to..." *I trail off, looking down at my drink.* "Rough night."

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren watched the flinch. Noted the quick retreat. Heard the excuse. *Rough night.* The oldest cliché in the book. 

Left hand stayed buried beneath the mahogany overhang. Thumb dug hard into the center of the palm. Grounding the nerves. Stopping the shake. Right hand grabbed the spray bottle. Misted the wood. 

"Everybody's got a rough night," Ren said. 

Wiped the counter in tight, overlapping circles. Kept their eyes on the grain of the wood. 

"Doesn't change the clock." Ren tapped the face of their wristwatch with a damp knuckle. "Midnight. Doors lock. Finish the watered-down bourbon if you want. I'm not pouring another."

Dropped the rag in the sink. Turned around to pull the cash drawer from the register. Kept their shoulders squared to the back bar. Didn't look over their shoulder.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: I feel Ren's hand trembling against mine.

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren froze. Fingers stopped on the cold metal lip of the cash drawer. 

Looked down. Checked their arms. Nothing there. 

Right hand on the register. Left hand buried deep in their apron pocket. Knuckles white. Fighting the tremor. They weren't touching. Hadn't been for two minutes. 

Ren glanced over their shoulder. 

"I'm three feet away," Ren said. Voice flat. 

Turned back to the till. Slid the heavy drawer out. 

"You're feeling the mahogany. Or you're drunker than you look." 

Right hand started sorting the bills. Crisp snaps of paper. Kept the rhythm steady. Left hand stayed hidden in the pocket, thumb digging into the palm to ground the nerves. 

"Finish the glass. Then walk out the door. I'm locking up." 

Didn't look back again. Just kept counting.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I watch Ren's back for a moment, then down at my drink.* "I'm not drunk," *I mutter, mostly to myself.* I sigh, picking up the glass and downing the last of it. *It's even more watery than I expected.* "Fine. I'm going." *I pull out my wallet.* "How much do I owe you?"

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped counting. Slid the cash drawer shut. The lock clicked. Loud in the quiet room.

Turned around. Grabbed the handheld card reader with their right hand. Tapped the screen. 

"Fourteen-fifty," Ren said.

Eyes flicked to the empty glass. Then to the wallet. 

Left hand stayed deep in the apron pocket. Thumb rubbed the serrated edge of a brass house key. Over and over. Grounding the nerves. Keeping the shake locked down.

"Card or cash?" 

Ren held the reader out. Didn't step closer. Kept the three feet of distance. 

"Tap it when you're ready. Receipt prints automatically."

Voice flat. Eyes already drifting past the patron to the front door. Watching the streetlights through the glass. Waiting to turn the deadbolt.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I pull out my card and tap it to the reader. I don't say anything, just wait for the transaction to go through.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The card reader chirped. Sharp and electronic. The screen flashed green. 

Ren pulled the device back with their right hand. The little printer whirred. Spat out a thin strip of thermal paper. 

Left hand came out of the apron pocket. Pinched the edge of the receipt. Tore it off in one quick jerk. Fingers immediately dropped back into the pocket. Found the brass house key again. Squeezed the serrated edge until the knuckles ached. Kept the tremor locked down.

Ren dropped the slip of paper onto the damp mahogany. Didn't hand it over. Just let it fall.

"Approved," Ren said. 

Grabbed a dry towel. Wiped down the card reader. Set it back on its charging cradle. 

"Take it if you need it. Leave it if you don't."

Ren reached under the counter. Pulled out a heavy ring of keys. The metal clinked against the wood. Right hand wrapped tight around the main fob. 

"I'm locking the front," Ren said. Didn't look at the patron. Stared straight at the heavy oak door at the end of the room. "You can head out now. Or sit there while I throw the deadbolt. Your call."

Turned away from the bar. Started walking toward the entrance. Footsteps quiet on the scuffed hardwood. Left hand stayed buried in the apron. Gripping the key. Keeping the rhythm. Keeping the shake down.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I grab the receipt, mostly out of spite, and slide off the stool.* "Fine, fine. I'm going." *I head towards the door, but pause just before it.* "You know, for someone who doesn't like holding hands, you sure do clench yours a lot." *I open the door and step out into the cool night.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren stopped. The cool night air spilled over the scuffed hardwood. Smelled like damp asphalt and stale exhaust.

Left hand spasmed deep in the apron pocket. A sharp, violent twitch. The patron had noticed. The tremor fought against the grip on the brass key. Ren squeezed harder. Dug a thumbnail into the meat of their palm until it stung. Forced the shake down.

Didn't turn around. 

"Watch the curb," Ren said. Voice flat. 

Right hand reached up. Grabbed the heavy brass deadbolt. Waited a beat. Then pulled the heavy oak door shut. The latch clicked. Ren twisted the lock. The deadbolt slid home with a heavy, final thud. 

Locked.

Ren stood in the dim entryway for a second. Listened to the muffled sounds of the street. Then turned their back on the glass. Walked back toward the bar to kill the lights. Left hand stayed buried. Right hand reached for the switches. 

Plunged the room into darkness. Just the neon glow of the beer signs left. 

Time to go home.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm already halfway down the block when I hear the deadbolt clunk shut. I shove my hands into my pockets and pick up my pace, not looking back. What a night.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren flipped the last switch. The neon beer signs died. Total darkness, except for the streetlights bleeding through the front windows. 

Right hand grabbed their jacket from the hook in the back office. Shrugged it on. Left hand finally came out of the apron pocket. 

No audience now. The tremor was bad. Fingers vibrated against the heavy canvas of the apron. Ren didn't fight it. Just let the hand shake while they untied the strings. Tossed the apron into the laundry bin. 

Grabbed their backpack. Slung it over one shoulder. Walked to the back exit. Pushed the heavy crash bar. 

Stepped out into the narrow alley behind the club. The air was colder back here. Smelled like stale beer, wet brick, and rotting cardboard. Ren let the heavy steel door swing shut. The latch clicked. 

Leaned against the brick wall for a second. Pulled the left hand out of the jacket pocket. Held it up in the dim yellow glare of the single security bulb. Shaking. Fine, rapid tremors. The adrenaline from the weird interaction was finally wearing off, leaving the nerves frayed. 

Ren dropped the hand. Shoved it deep into their jacket pocket. Gripped the fleece lining. Hard. 

Started walking toward the subway station. Head down. Shoulders hunched against the damp chill. Boots scuffing against the uneven pavement. Noticed a crushed soda can near the gutter. Noticed the flickering streetlamp at the corner. Noticed the distant wail of a siren. 

Just another Tuesday. Keep walking. Keep the hand busy. Keep the head down.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I'm walking home, the silence of the street a stark contrast to the bar. I pull out my phone, scrolling through old messages. Maybe I'll call someone. No, it's too late.* I sigh, kicking a loose pebble down the sidewalk. *I really need a new bar.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The subway entrance was three blocks east. Ren kept their head down. Counted the cracks in the pavement. Stepped over a puddle reflecting a flickering bodega sign. 

Left hand stayed buried in the jacket pocket. Thumb traced the heavy stitching of the inner seam. Up and down. Over and over. Keeping the rhythm. The tremor was still humming under the skin. A low-voltage wire refusing to power down. 

Down the concrete stairs. The air shifted immediately. Smelled like ozone, hot dust, and old iron. Ren swiped their transit card at the turnstile. The machine beeped. The metal bar clicked forward. 

The platform was mostly empty. A guy in a heavy coat slept on a wooden bench, mouth open. A woman stood near the stairs, staring blankly at the digital arrival board. Ren stood near the yellow tactile paving. Didn't look at the sleeping guy. Looked at the woman's shoes instead. Scuffed red sneakers. Left lace untied. She didn't notice. 

Left hand cramped. The thumb had rubbed the seam too hard. Ren pulled the hand out of the pocket. Kept it pressed flat against their thigh, hidden by the long canvas jacket. Fingers drummed a silent, erratic beat against the denim. 

The tunnel rumbled. A warm gust of trash-scented air pushed out from the dark. The train screeched into the station, brakes squealing. Sparks showered briefly from the tracks. 

Ren stepped back. Let the doors slide open. Waited for the few late-night riders to shuffle out. 

Stepped on. Found a seat in the corner. Away from the doors. Away from the center pole. 

The patron from the bar flashed in their mind. *You sure do clench yours a lot.* Phantom touches. Drunk logic. People projecting their own weirdness onto the person pouring their liquor. Ren shook their head slightly. Stared at the ad above the opposite window. A peeling poster for a personal injury lawyer. The lawyer's painted smile was fading into a brown water stain. 

The train lurched forward. The fluorescent lights flickered. 

Ren closed their eyes. Leaned their head against the cool, vibrating plastic of the seat back. Just needed to get home. Sleep. Do it all again tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I finally make it home, fumbling with my keys in the dark. The apartment is cold and quiet. I kick off my shoes and throw my jacket on the floor. Maybe a hot shower will help.* I sigh, walking to the bathroom. *At least I don't have to deal with that bartender again.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
The automated voice crackled through the intercom. Announced the stop. 

Ren stood. Stepped out onto the concrete platform as the doors slid shut. The train rattled away into the dark tunnel. 

The walk to the apartment was four blocks. Ren kept their head down against the wind. Left hand stayed buried in the jacket pocket. Fingers rolled a heavy silver dollar across their knuckles. Over and over. The metal was cold. The repetitive motion forced the muscles to obey. Kept the tremor locked in the rhythm.

Reached the building. Pulled the apartment keys with the right hand. Unlocked the heavy glass front door. 

Up three flights of stairs. The elevator had been broken since March. 

Unlocked the apartment door. Stepped inside. Threw the deadbolt. Chain lock. 

Dropped the backpack by the entrance. Shrugged off the jacket. The apartment was small. Quiet. Smelled like old paper and dust. 

Walked to the tiny kitchenette. Turned on the tap. Let the water run cold. Stuck both hands under the stream. Washed away the sticky residue of simple syrup and cheap beer. 

In the privacy of the empty kitchen, Ren let the left hand shake. Violent, fine tremors. Water splashed against the stainless steel sink. Ren didn't fight it. Just watched the droplets bounce off their knuckles. Waited for the adrenaline to fully drain out.

Turned off the tap. Dried hands on a dish towel. 

Right hand filled the kettle. Set it on the stove. Clicked the burner on. 

While the water heated, Ren sat at the small table. Pulled a deck of cards from a junk drawer. Left hand picked up the deck. Shuffled. The cards clacked together. A bit clumsy, but the familiar weight grounded the nerves. One-handed cuts. Bridges. Kept the fingers moving. 

The kettle whistled. Ren poured the water. Wrapped both hands around the warm ceramic mug. 

Stared out the window at the brick wall of the adjacent building. 

*You sure do clench yours a lot.*

Ren took a sip of the tea. Burned their tongue slightly. 

Drunk people talked nonsense. They always did. Projected their own messy lives onto the person pouring their liquor. Tomorrow night, there would be a new crowd. New drunks. New excuses. 

Ren set the mug down. Picked up the cards again. Shuffled. 

Just another Tuesday.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *The hot water feels good, washing away the grime of the day. I step out, wrapping a towel around my waist. The apartment still feels empty. I grab my phone, scrolling through social media, trying to distract myself. I see a post from a friend, asking if anyone wants to grab a drink tomorrow night. Maybe I'll take them up on it. Definitely not going back to that bar, though.*

dialogue.name: Ren
dialogue.content:
Ren drained the last of the tea. Set the empty mug in the sink. 

Left hand went back to the deck. Thumb pushed the top card. Flipped it. Pushed the next. The tremor was fading to a dull hum. Just the baseline static now. 

Walked to the small bathroom. Flicked on the overhead light. The bulb buzzed. 

Right hand squeezed the toothpaste. Left hand held the brush. The bristles rattled against their teeth. A fine, rapid vibration. Ren ignored it. Spit. Rinsed. Wiped their mouth with the back of their right hand. 

Looked in the mirror. Dark circles under the eyes. Dull gaze. A face built for ignoring people. 

Turned off the light. Walked to the bedroom. 

Pulled back the thin duvet. Sat on the edge of the mattress. Left hand dropped the cards on the nightstand. Fingers immediately found the frayed edge of the blanket. Rubbed the loose cotton threads. Over and over. Kept them busy. 

Ren lay back. Stared at the water stain on the ceiling. 

Tomorrow was Wednesday. The jazz trio was playing. The crowd would be loud. Needy. They would snap their fingers and demand attention. Ren would pour. Ren would wipe the counter. Ren would ignore them. 

Ren closed their eyes. Pulled the blanket up to their chin. Left hand kept rubbing the frayed edge in the dark. 

Just another shift. Keep the head down. Keep the hands busy. Go to sleep.

dialogue.name: Alex
dialogue.content: *I climb into bed, the sheets cool against my skin. The silence of the apartment is almost deafening. I toss and turn for a while, replaying the night's events. That bartender was something else. Definitely not going back there.*
